instructions.you: You are an account executive on a friendly video call with a customer. Warm, relaxed, confident, natural conversational pace. Not salesy.
instructions.them: You are Dana, head of operations at a fast-growing startup, on a video call with a vendor. Friendly but direct and businesslike, natural conversational pace.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Hi Dana, thanks for making time today.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Of course. Good timing, actually. We have a lot going on.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Before we get into the renewal, how are things at Acme? Last time we talked, you were in the middle of fundraising.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Right, we closed our Series B two weeks ago. Thirty-two million, led by Northstar. So we’re hiring fast.
lines.display: Right, we closed our Series B two weeks ago. $32 million, led by Northstar. So we’re hiring fast.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Congratulations! How does that change your team size?

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Support goes from forty people to about a hundred and ten by March. With ops and success, call it a hundred and twenty seats.
lines.display: Support goes from 40 people to about 110 by March. With ops and success, call it 120 seats.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: So roughly triple. Would everyone be in the platform every day?

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Most of them. About twenty are managers who only need the dashboards.
lines.display: Most of them. About 20 are managers who only need the dashboards.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: We have a viewer seat for exactly that, and it’s priced much lower.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Good, because pricing is my main concern. At sixty-five dollars a seat, a hundred and twenty seats is a big jump, and my CFO will push back.
lines.display: Good, because pricing is my main concern. At $65 a seat, 120 seats is a big jump, and my CFO will push back.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: That’s fair. At that volume you’d move to our growth tier, and a multi-year term usually brings the per-seat price down quite a bit.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: A two-year term could work. But I need year one under ninety thousand.
lines.display: A two-year term could work. But I need year one under $90K.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Understood. I’ll send two options, annual and two-year, with the viewer seats broken out.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Perfect. The other thing is security. Every vendor now goes through a formal review with our new CISO, Marcus.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: No problem. I can send our SOC 2 Type Two report and a completed security questionnaire.
lines.display: No problem. I can send our SOC 2 Type II report and a completed security questionnaire.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: He’ll also ask about single sign-on. We need SSO through Okta before we roll out to everyone.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Okta SSO is included on the growth tier. I can also set up a call with our security lead if Marcus wants to go deeper.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Let’s do that. He’s free Tuesday afternoon.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: Great. So, to recap: both pricing options and the SOC 2 report from me by Thursday, and a security call with Marcus on Tuesday.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Sounds right. Our contract ends on the thirtieth, so I’d like to sign before then.
lines.display: Sounds right. Our contract ends on the 30th, so I’d like to sign before then.

lines.speaker: you
lines.text: That works. Thanks, Dana, this was really helpful.

lines.speaker: them
lines.text: Thanks. Talk soon.
